thread:
Alice: heads up — we're seeing a burst of 502/504s from model-puller in us-east-1. latency spikes and a bunch of `connect` errors. looks like egress issues across multiple AZs :eyes:
Ben: seeing it too. a bunch of pods failing to open outbound sockets. quick grep from sidecar logs: ```
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z model-puller sidecar ERROR: dial tcp: connect: cannot assign requested address
2026-03-18T09:12:04Z model-puller sidecar WARN: listen tcp: address already in use
```
Carla: NAT gateway metrics for us-east-1a/us-east-1b show SNATConnectionUtilization ~100% and elevated ConnectionCount. Also saw lots of short-lived connections from model-puller + telemetry fanout. This matches ephemeral port exhaustion.
Darren: putting a quick incident note in #incidents. tagging oncall. :fire:
deploy-bot: incident created: INC-2026-032 (egress-nat-saturation-us-east-1) — paging oncall.
Alice: first-order mitigation ideas — reduce parallel model pulls, enable HTTP keepalive on sidecar, add per-AZ NATs or temporary NAT instances for burst. Thoughts?
Ben: agree. quick patch to sidecar to enable connection reuse is low-risk. patch: ```yaml
env:
  - name: HTTP_KEEPALIVE
    value: "true"
````
Carla: also can we modify kube-svc egress policy to prefer AZ-local NATs? currently nodes route to a single shared NAT pair in the account. If we spin up additional NAT gateways/instances in each AZ we can reduce cross-AZ SNAT contention.
Alice: spinning up 1 NAT instance in us-east-1a now to relieve hot AZ (temp measure). aws cli: `aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-nat --instance-type t3.micro --subnet-id subnet-xx --associate-public-ip-address` then configure iptables SNAT.
Ben: added a rolling patch to model-puller deployment to cap concurrent downloads: `MAX_PARALLEL_PULLS=4`. deploying now.
Carla: also disabled telemetry fanout for model-puller (set TELEMETRY_FANOUT=false) while we triage.
Darren: after the patch, connection errors dropped from 1200/min to ~40/min in 10m. NAT ConnectionCount on gw-xyz decreased accordingly. looks promising. :thumbsup:
Alice: good — need a durable fix: options we discussed: 1) enforce connection pooling/keepalive in sidecars 2) more NAT per AZ or use NAT instances with larger ephemeral port range 3) introduce an egress proxy cluster (long-lived connections) 4) tune client side (reuse sockets, DNS caching)
Ben: on the egress proxy idea — envoy cluster with pool of outbound sockets would massively reduce ephemeral port churn. Worth prototyping.
Carla: quick experiment results: enabling HTTP_KEEPALIVE cut ephemeral allocation rate by ~70% for a test workload. logs: ```
Before: 500 new SNAT ports/min
After: 140 new SNAT ports/min
```
Alice: ok next actions: 
- ben: roll out keepalive + MAX_PARALLEL_PULLS to all model-puller pods (in progress)
- carla: open infra task to add per-AZ NAT gateways and estimate cost impact
- darren: write temporary runbook for incident responders (how to detect SNAT exhaustion, when to spin NAT instances)
- alice: start prototype for egress-proxy (envoy) and test perf/cost

Darren: creating ticket INFRA-492: "per-AZ-nat-and-egress-proxy-recommendation" and assigning to eng-infra. ETA EOW for proposal.
Ben: note for postmortem — telemetry fanout should have a circuit breaker to prevent stampedes. Adding to infra backlog.
Alice: resolved-notice — immediate user-facing errors reduced, increased NAT capacity + sidecar connection reuse helped. will monitor for 24h.
deploy-bot: deployment model-puller v3.2.1 rolled out to 60% traffic — checks green.
Carla: monitoring shows stable SNAT utilization across AZs now. we'll keep the temporary NAT instance until proper per-AZ NATs are provisioned.
Alice: retrospective tasks: doc runbook + add dashboards for SNATConnectionUtilization per-gateway + alert when ephemeral port allocation rate > threshold. Also add kb: `how to detect ephemeral port exhaustion` with sample `ss` commands and common log patterns.
Darren: thanks everyone — great cross-team response. will schedule a postmortem tomorrow 11am PT. :calendar:
Alice: tagging followups: @ben @carla @darren — please add check-ins to INFRA-492 and close when complete.
Carla: adding checklist now.
Ben: one-liner for the postmortem: cause = high parallel outbound short-lived connections (model pulls + telemetry) -> NAT SNAT port exhaustion -> connection resets and 5xx. mitigations = connection reuse, cap parallelism, per-AZ egress capacity, egress proxy.
Alice: closing thread for now — monitoring only.
